options: A material that lets charge flow easily
A device that stores chemical energy
A material that blocks electric charge
insulator.hint: The answer is "A material that blocks electric charge". Insulators do not let electric charge move through them.

insulator.q: Which statement about insulators is true?
options: They are always made of metal.
They do not let electric charge move through them.
They make electric charge move faster.
insulator.hint: The answer is "They do not let electric charge move through them.". Insulators stop electric charge from moving through them.

insulator.q: Fill in the blank: An insulator does not let electric ___ move through it.
insulator.hint: The answer is "charge". Insulators block the flow of electric charge.

insulator.q: Which word means 'a material that does not let electric charge move through it'?
insulator.hint: The answer is "Insulator". That is the meaning of insulator.

insulator.q: Which word is the opposite of an electrical insulator?
insulator.hint: The answer is "Conductor". Conductors let charge flow; insulators do not.

insulator.q: Which material is an electrical insulator?
insulator.hint: The answer is "Rubber". Rubber does not let electric charge move through it.

insulator.q: Which spoon is NOT an electrical insulator?
insulator.hint: The answer is "A metal spoon". Metal lets charge flow, so it is not an insulator.
The answer is "Rubber, wood, glass". Rubber, wood, and glass all block electric charge.

insulator.q: Which item belongs in the insulator pile?
insulator.hint: The answer is "A glass marble". Glass is an insulator; metals are conductors.

insulator.q: Which one does NOT belong with plastic, wood, and glass?
insulator.hint: The answer is "A steel paper clip". Steel is a metal that lets charge flow.

insulator.q: Electricians wear gloves to stay safe from electricity. What should the gloves be made of?
insulator.hint: The answer is "Rubber". Rubber is an insulator, so charge cannot reach the hand.

insulator.q: Why do lamp cords have a plastic coating on the outside?
options: To block charge so it is safe to touch
insulator.hint: The answer is "To block charge so it is safe to touch". Plastic is an insulator that keeps the charge inside.

insulator.q: Maya puts a wooden stick into a gap in her circuit. What happens to the bulb?
insulator.hint: The answer is "It stays off". Wood is an insulator, so energy cannot flow across the gap.

insulator.q: Sam tests a glass rod, a rubber eraser, and a plastic straw in a circuit. None of them light the bulb. What are they?
insulator.hint: The answer is "Insulators". They all block electric charge, so they are insulators.

insulator.q: Which tool should a worker use to fix a power line?
options: A tool with bare metal handles
A tool wrapped in a wet cloth
insulator.hint: The answer is "A tool with rubber handles". Rubber is an insulator; metal and water let charge flow.

options: A complete path for electrical energy
circuit.hint: The answer is "A complete path for electrical energy". A circuit is a complete path through which electrical energy can flow.

circuit.q: Which statement about circuits is true?
options: A circuit works best with a gap in it.
A circuit needs no energy source.
Electrical energy flows through a complete path.
circuit.hint: The answer is "Electrical energy flows through a complete path.". Energy can only flow when the path is complete.

circuit.q: Fill in the blank: A circuit is a complete ___ through which electrical energy can flow.
circuit.hint: The answer is "path". A circuit is a complete path.

circuit.q: Which word means 'a complete path through which electrical energy can flow'?
circuit.hint: The answer is "Circuit". That is the meaning of circuit.

circuit.q: What kind of energy flows through the wires of a circuit?
circuit.hint: The answer is "Electrical energy". Circuits carry electrical energy.

circuit.q: Which is an example of a complete circuit?
options: Battery, wires, and bulb connected in a loop
A bulb sitting alone on a desk
A battery lying in a drawer
circuit.hint: The answer is "Battery, wires, and bulb connected in a loop". The parts are joined in a full loop, so energy can flow.

circuit.q: Which set of parts could make a simple circuit that lights a bulb?
circuit.hint: The answer is "Battery, wires, bulb". A battery, wires, and a bulb can make a complete path.

circuit.q: Which object has a circuit inside it?
circuit.hint: The answer is "A flashlight". A flashlight has a battery, wires, a switch, and a bulb.

circuit.q: Which is NOT a part of a simple circuit?
circuit.hint: The answer is "A pencil eraser". Wires and batteries are circuit parts; an eraser is not.

circuit.q: Leo wants to connect a battery to a bulb to make a circuit. What should he use for the path?
circuit.hint: The answer is "Copper wire". Copper is metal, so it can complete the path.

circuit.q: Liam connects a battery to a bulb with only one wire. The bulb stays dark. Why?
options: The battery has too much energy
circuit.hint: The answer is "The path is not complete". Energy needs a complete loop to flow.

circuit.q: Mia builds a circuit with a battery, wires, and a bulb. When it works, what does the bulb give off?
circuit.hint: The answer is "Light". A bulb changes electrical energy into light.

circuit.q: Why must the parts inside a flashlight be connected in a loop?
options: So energy has a complete path
circuit.hint: The answer is "So energy has a complete path". Electrical energy flows only through a complete path.

circuit.q: At the science fair, Ava's circuit lights a bulb. She removes one wire. What will happen?
circuit.hint: The answer is "The bulb goes out". Removing a wire breaks the path, so energy stops.

circuit.q: Ben is building a circuit. What should he use to connect the parts?
circuit.hint: The answer is "Metal wire". Metal wire carries electrical energy.

options: A complete path that lets energy flow
A broken path that stops energy
closed.hint: The answer is "A complete path that lets energy flow". A closed circuit is a complete path.

closed.q: In a closed circuit with a bulb, what happens to the light?
closed.hint: The answer is "It turns on". Energy flows in a closed circuit, so the light turns on.

closed.q: Fill in the blank: A closed circuit is a ___ path that allows electrical energy to flow.
closed.hint: The answer is "complete". Closed means the path is complete.

closed.q: Which term means 'a complete path that allows electrical energy to flow'?
closed.hint: The answer is "Closed circuit". A closed circuit has no gaps.

closed.q: Which statement about a closed circuit is true?
options: Energy can flow all the way around.
There is a gap in the path.
closed.hint: The answer is "Energy can flow all the way around.". With no gaps, energy flows all the way around.

closed.q: Which is an example of a closed circuit?
closed.hint: The answer is "A flashlight that is shining". The flashlight is shining, so its path is complete.

closed.q: Which is NOT a closed circuit?
options: A lamp with a cut wire
closed.hint: The answer is "A lamp with a cut wire". A cut wire breaks the path.

options: A toaster unplugged on the counter
A TV that is on and playing
closed.hint: The answer is "A TV that is on and playing". The TV is working, so energy is flowing.

closed.q: Which group are all closed circuits?
options: Lit lamp, unplugged fan, playing radio
Flashlight with no battery, lit lamp, spinning fan
Lit lamp, spinning fan, playing radio
closed.hint: The answer is "Lit lamp, spinning fan, playing radio". Each one is working, so each path is complete.
The answer is "The light turns on". In a closed circuit, the light turns on.

closed.q: Zoe flips her bedroom light switch and the light comes on. What kind of circuit is it now?
closed.hint: The answer is "Closed circuit". The light is on, so the path is complete.

closed.q: Jake hooks up a battery, wires, and a bulb, and the bulb glows. Why?
options: The wire is made of rubber
closed.hint: The answer is "The path is complete". A complete path lets electrical energy flow.

closed.q: A fan is spinning in the classroom. What is true about its circuit?
options: There is a gap in the wire
closed.hint: The answer is "Electrical energy is flowing". The fan works because the circuit is closed.

closed.q: Ella's circuit has a gap. She fills the gap with a metal paper clip. What will happen?
closed.hint: The answer is "The bulb lights up". The metal clip completes the path.

closed.q: Kai wants his toy car's motor to run. What kind of circuit does he need?
closed.hint: The answer is "A closed circuit". Energy flows only in a closed circuit.

options: A complete path that lets energy flow
A broken path that stops energy flow
open.hint: The answer is "A broken path that stops energy flow". An open circuit has a break in the path.

open.q: What does an open circuit do to electrical energy?
open.hint: The answer is "Stops it from flowing". A broken path stops electrical energy.

open.q: Fill in the blank: An open circuit is a broken or ___ path.
open.hint: The answer is "incomplete". Open circuits are broken or incomplete.

open.q: Which term means 'a broken path that stops electrical energy from flowing'?
open.hint: The answer is "Open circuit". That is the meaning of open circuit.

open.q: Which statement about an open circuit is true?
options: A bulb in it will not light.
It makes a bulb glow brightly.
open.hint: The answer is "A bulb in it will not light.". No energy flows, so the bulb stays off.

open.q: Which is an example of an open circuit?
options: A lamp with a broken wire
open.hint: The answer is "A lamp with a broken wire". The broken wire makes the path incomplete.

open.q: Which is NOT an open circuit?
open.hint: The answer is "A glowing light bulb". A glowing bulb means energy is flowing.

open.q: Which situation makes an open circuit?
options: A wire falls off the battery
A paper clip fills the gap
open.hint: The answer is "A wire falls off the battery". A loose wire leaves a gap in the path.
The answer is "The light is off". In an open circuit, energy cannot reach the light.

open.q: Which group shows only open circuits?
options: Cut wire, loose battery, switch off
Cut wire, lit lamp, switch off
Lit lamp, running fan, switch on
open.hint: The answer is "Cut wire, loose battery, switch off". Each one has a break in the path.

open.q: Noah's flashlight won't turn on. He finds a wire came loose. What kind of circuit is it?
open.hint: The answer is "Open circuit". The loose wire breaks the path.

open.q: Lily puts a rubber eraser in the gap of her circuit. What will happen?
open.hint: The answer is "The bulb stays off". Rubber is an insulator, so the circuit stays open.

open.q: A string of lights goes dark when one wire breaks. Why?
options: The path is no longer complete
open.hint: The answer is "The path is no longer complete". A broken wire makes an open circuit.

open.q: Dad unplugs the toaster. What happens to the flow of electrical energy to it?
open.hint: The answer is "It stops". Unplugging breaks the path.

open.q: Mr. Lee wants a buzzer in a class circuit to stop without breaking anything. What should he do?
open.hint: The answer is "Disconnect one wire". Disconnecting a wire opens the circuit.

options: A device that stores chemical energy
A device that opens or closes a circuit
switch.hint: The answer is "A device that opens or closes a circuit". A switch opens or closes an electrical circuit.

switch.q: What two things can a switch do to a circuit?
switch.hint: The answer is "Open it or close it". A switch opens or closes the path.

switch.q: Fill in the blank: A switch is a device that opens or ___ an electrical circuit.
switch.hint: The answer is "closes". A switch opens or closes a circuit.

switch.q: Which word means 'a device that opens or closes an electrical circuit'?
switch.hint: The answer is "Switch". That is the meaning of switch.

switch.q: Which statement about switches is true?
options: Turning a switch off opens the circuit.
A switch is a kind of battery.
switch.hint: The answer is "Turning a switch off opens the circuit.". Off makes a gap, so the circuit is open.

switch.q: Which is an example of a switch?
options: A light switch on the wall
switch.hint: The answer is "A light switch on the wall". A wall light switch opens and closes the circuit.
The answer is "A copper wire". A wire carries energy; it does not open or close the circuit.

switch.q: Which part of a flashlight is the switch?
switch.hint: The answer is "The on/off button". The button opens and closes the flashlight's circuit.

switch.q: Which is an example of a switch closing a circuit?
options: Flipping a lamp switch to on
switch.hint: The answer is "Flipping a lamp switch to on". Turning the switch on completes the path.

switch.q: Which is an example of a switch opening a circuit?
switch.hint: The answer is "Turning a fan switch off". Turning the switch off breaks the path.

switch.q: Emma flips her light switch and the light turns on. What did the switch do?
switch.hint: The answer is "Closed the circuit". The switch completed the path so energy could flow.

switch.q: When you press the off button on a fan, why does it stop?
options: The fan runs out of air
switch.hint: The answer is "The switch opens the circuit". Opening the circuit stops the energy flow.

switch.q: Leo wants to turn his bulb on and off without unhooking wires. What should he add?
switch.hint: The answer is "A switch". A switch opens and closes the circuit.

switch.q: At the science fair, Ana's circuit switch is in the off position. What will the bulb do?
switch.hint: The answer is "Stay off". Off means the circuit is open, so no energy flows.

switch.q: A doorbell rings only while its button is pushed. What happens when you let go?
options: The circuit opens and it stops
The circuit closes and it rings louder
switch.hint: The answer is "The circuit opens and it stops". Letting go of the button opens the circuit.

wire.q: What does a wire do in a circuit?
wire.hint: The answer is "Carries electrical energy". A wire carries electrical energy in a circuit.

wire.q: What is a wire usually made of?
wire.hint: The answer is "Metal covered in plastic". Wires are usually metal covered in plastic.

wire.q: Fill in the blank: A wire is a material that ___ electrical energy in a circuit.
wire.hint: The answer is "carries". Wires carry electrical energy.

wire.q: Which word means 'a material that carries electrical energy in a circuit'?
wire.hint: The answer is "Wire". That is the meaning of wire.

wire.q: Which statement about wires is true?
options: The plastic outside carries the energy.
The metal inside carries the energy.
wire.hint: The answer is "The metal inside carries the energy.". Metal lets energy flow; the plastic is an insulator.

wire.q: Which is an example of a wire?
wire.hint: The answer is "A phone charger cord". A charger cord is metal wire covered in plastic.

wire.q: Which could work as a wire in a simple circuit?
wire.hint: The answer is "A strip of aluminum foil". Foil is metal, so it can carry electrical energy.

wire.q: Which is NOT a good material for the inside of a wire?
wire.hint: The answer is "Plastic". Plastic is an insulator, so it is used on the outside.

wire.q: Which household thing has wires inside it?
wire.hint: The answer is "A toaster". A toaster uses wires to carry electrical energy.
The answer is "A rubber eraser". Rubber cannot carry electrical energy.

wire.q: Why is the copper inside a lamp cord covered in plastic?
options: So it is safe to touch
wire.hint: The answer is "So it is safe to touch". The plastic is an insulator that keeps people safe.

wire.q: Sam sees a cord with torn plastic and metal showing. What should he do?
options: Tell an adult and not touch it
wire.hint: The answer is "Tell an adult and not touch it". Bare metal wire is unsafe; water conducts electricity too.

wire.q: In a flashlight, what carries energy from the battery to the bulb?
wire.hint: The answer is "Metal wires or strips". Metal carries electrical energy; plastic and glass do not.

wire.q: At the science fair, Ravi cuts the only wire in his circuit in half. What will happen?
wire.hint: The answer is "The bulb goes out". A cut wire cannot carry energy to the bulb.

wire.q: Grace connects a bulb to a battery using long wires instead of short ones. Will energy still reach the bulb?
options: No, wires only work when short
wire.hint: The answer is "Yes, the wires carry it". Wires carry electrical energy along their length.

options: Stores chemical energy, gives electrical energy
battery.hint: The answer is "Stores chemical energy, gives electrical energy". A battery stores chemical energy and provides electrical energy.

battery.q: Which statement about batteries is true?
options: A battery is an energy source for a circuit.
battery.hint: The answer is "A battery is an energy source for a circuit.". A battery provides electrical energy to a circuit.

battery.q: Fill in the blank: A battery stores chemical energy and provides ___ energy.
battery.hint: The answer is "electrical". Batteries give electrical energy.

battery.q: Which word means 'a device that stores chemical energy and provides electrical energy'?
battery.hint: The answer is "Battery". That is the meaning of battery.

battery.q: What kind of energy is stored inside a battery?
battery.hint: The answer is "Chemical energy". A battery stores chemical energy.
The answer is "A TV remote". A TV remote uses batteries for energy.
The answer is "A light bulb". A light bulb uses energy; it does not store it.

battery.q: Which group is all powered by batteries?
battery.hint: The answer is "Flashlight, TV remote, remote-control car". All three use batteries.

battery.q: Which is an example of a battery giving energy?
options: A lamp plugged into the wall
battery.hint: The answer is "A phone working while unplugged". The phone's battery provides electrical energy.

battery.q: Which part of a watch is the battery?
battery.hint: The answer is "The small round cell inside". The small cell stores chemical energy.

battery.q: Kim's flashlight gets dim after many hours of use. Why?
battery.hint: The answer is "Its battery is running low". The battery's stored chemical energy is getting used.

battery.q: Owen's remote-control car stops working. What should he try first?
battery.hint: The answer is "Put in new batteries". New batteries provide energy again.

battery.q: A battery powers a flashlight. Which energy chain is correct?
battery.hint: The answer is "Chemical -> electrical -> light". The battery's chemical energy becomes electrical, then light.

battery.q: At the science fair, Jade builds a circuit with wires and a bulb but no battery. What will happen?
battery.hint: The answer is "The bulb stays dark". Without a battery, there is no energy source.

battery.q: Why can a radio with batteries play music at the beach with no outlet?
options: The batteries store energy it carries along
battery.hint: The answer is "The batteries store energy it carries along". Batteries store chemical energy to provide electrical energy.

options: A machine that changes electrical energy into another form
A path for energy to flow
device.hint: The answer is "A machine that changes electrical energy into another form". Devices change electrical energy into other forms.

device.q: What kind of energy goes into a plugged-in electrical device?
device.hint: The answer is "Electrical energy". Devices take in electrical energy.

device.q: Fill in the blank: An electrical device changes electrical energy into another ___ of energy.
device.hint: The answer is "form". Devices change energy into another form.

device.q: Which term means 'a machine that changes electrical energy into another form of energy'?
device.hint: The answer is "Electrical device". That is the meaning of electrical device.
The answer is "Speaker -> sound". A speaker changes electrical energy into sound.
The answer is "A toaster". A toaster changes electrical energy into heat.

device.q: Which is NOT an electrical device?
device.hint: The answer is "A pencil". A pencil does not use electrical energy.

device.q: Which device is used to make heat?
device.hint: The answer is "A toaster". A toaster changes electrical energy into heat.

device.q: Which device is used to make motion?
device.hint: The answer is "A fan". A fan changes electrical energy into motion.

device.q: Which group has only devices made to give light?
device.hint: The answer is "Lamp, flashlight, night-light". Lamps, flashlights, and night-lights all make light.

device.q: Ruby plugs in a speaker to play music. What energy goes in and what comes out?
device.hint: The answer is "Electrical in, sound out". A speaker changes electrical energy into sound.

device.q: On a hot day, Max turns on a fan. What energy does the fan mainly give?
device.hint: The answer is "Motion energy". A fan changes electrical energy into motion.

device.q: Mom makes toast. What energy goes into the toaster and what comes out?
device.hint: The answer is "Electrical in, heat out". A toaster changes electrical energy into heat.

device.q: Ivy touches a lamp that has been on for an hour. It feels warm. Why?
options: Some electrical energy always becomes heat
device.hint: The answer is "Some electrical energy always becomes heat". Energy never changes completely into one form; some becomes heat.

device.q: In class, Ms. Kay turns on a hair dryer and it blows warm air. Which energy forms come out?
device.hint: The answer is "Heat and motion". The dryer makes heat and moving air.
